pamphlet_excerpts: Briefly discuss the historical origin: The groups, and many of the breeds within these groups, recognized by the AKC are as follows (p. 12).

Briefly discuss the historical origin Principle 2: These are dogs that "scent" and either track, point, or flush (reveal a bird's location and cause it to fly), and retrieve game birds on land or in water (p. 12).
Briefly discuss the historical origin Principle 3: The wide range of shape, size, color, and personality of purebred dogs is the result of controlled breeding and selection (p. 12).
Briefly discuss the historical origin Principle 4: Some dogs were bred to hunt, some to serve as guard or sled dogs, and some to be herders (p. 12).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Briefly discuss the historical origin): In the late 1800s, at the same time that dog shows we regaining popularity, a system was developed for classifying breeds according to how they are used (p. 12).
Step 2 (Briefly discuss the historical origin): In the United States, the American Kennel Club has maintained a registry of breeds since 1884 (p. 12).
Step 3 (Briefly discuss the historical origin): Recognized groups are sporting dogs, hounds, working dogs, terriers, toys, nonsporting dogs, and herding dogs (p. 12).
Step 4 (Briefly discuss the historical origin): Within these seven groups, the AKC recognizes 202 breeds (as of 2022, with new breeds being recognized every year) (p. 12).

B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
